chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Muhammad ibn 'Udhafir from 'Umar ibn Yazid from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When you enter the state of Ihram from Masjid al-Shajara, if you are walking, respond (with Talbiyah) from your place in the Masjid, saying: 'Here I am, O Allah, here I am, here I am, no partner is there for You, here I am, here I am, Possessor of the ascending paths, here I am, here I am, with a Hajj that is complete for You.' And proclaim it aloud whenever you mount, whenever you dismount, whenever you descend into a valley, or ascend a hill, or meet a rider, and in the early hours of the night."

key_terms.إِحْرَام: State of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.الْأَسْحَارِ: The early hours of the night/pre-dawn time
key_terms.ذَا الْمَعَارِجِ: Possessor of the ascending paths (an attribute of God in the Talbiyah)
key_terms.لَبَّيْكَ: The opening phrase of the Talbiyah supplication ('Here I am, O Allah')
key_terms.مَسْجِدُ الشَّجَرَةِ: Masjid al-Shajara, a specific Miqat (station of Ihram) near Mecca

ai.seo_question: How should a pilgrim recite the Talbiyah when leaving Masjid al-Shajara to begin Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the ritual precision of entering Ihram at Masjid al-Shajara, emphasizing the continuous and vocal recitation of the Talbiyah to maintain spiritual presence. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the physical acts of travel—mounting, descending, and traversing terrain—as opportunities for dhikr, reinforcing the pilgrimage as a holistic bodily and spiritual journey.
